purpose: Siponimod is used to treat secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. It helps slow down the worsening of disability and reduces the number of MS flare-ups. Your doctor may also use it for certain relapsing forms of MS.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks the protective coating around your nerves, causing MS symptoms. Siponimod works by keeping certain immune cells (called lymphocytes) trapped inside your lymph nodes so they cannot travel to your brain and spinal cord and cause damage. Think of it like redirecting troublemakers away from the neighborhood so they cannot cause harm.
common_side_effects: Headache, dizziness, high blood pressure, tiredness, nausea, swelling in your arms or legs, abnormal liver blood tests, and a temporary slowing of your heart rate especially when you first start the medication.
warnings: Before starting this medicine, you will need a blood test to check your genes (CYP2C9), an eye exam, heart monitoring, and vaccines may need to be updated. It can slow your heart rate when you first take it, so the first dose is usually taken under medical supervision. It can increase your risk of infections, including serious ones, so tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant as it can harm your baby. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication.
typical_dosing: You will start with a 5-day starter pack that gradually increases your dose from 0.25 mg up to the full maintenance dose of 2 mg once daily by mouth. After the starter pack, you take 2 mg every day. Always take it with or without food at the same time each day, and never skip doses without talking to your doctor first.
